reason: The hypothesis relies on SRO raising dislocation barriers (supported by E2, E5, E6) and SRO disordering under load enabling plasticity, but no cited evidence directly demonstrates that sustained loading disorders SRO at multilayer interfaces or that this disordering activates cooperative slip; these mechanistic links are inferred rather than empirically grounded.
premises: Chemical SRO raises the activation barrier for dislocation motion in HEAs
Sustained loading can progressively disorder SRO at HEA interfaces
SRO disordering activates cooperative dislocation slip and mediates plastic flow
Annealed HEA multilayers have higher initial SRO than as-deposited ones
SRO evolution can be monitored via electron diffraction and spectroscopy
